concepts.bodyMd:
The Adi-Hindu movement emerged in Hyderabad state to fight discrimination against Dalits, untouchability, and caste differences. **Madari Bhagya Reddy Varma** was the central figure behind this movement.

Bhagya Reddy Varma is regarded as the **Father of the Telangana Dalit Movement** and was named the **"Dalit Vaithalika."**

### Early Life

*   Born on **22nd May, 1888** into a "Mala" family in Hyderabad, to Madari Venkaiah and Rangamamba.
*   His original name was **Madari Bhagaiah**; his family guru renamed him Bhagya Reddy.
*   **Raavichettu Ranga Rao** financially supported his education.
*   He left home during childhood due to a family issue and joined a Roman Catholic Brothers' Tennis Court as a tennis ball boy, growing close to the Catholic Church family.
*   He later worked as an electrician in the electricity department, and subsequently joined the **Brahma Samaj** and **Arya Samaj**.

### Titles

| Title | Given By |
|---|---|
| Varma | Balaji Krishna Rao (Arya Samaj member, recognizing his services to Arya Samaj) |
| Shiva Shresta | Vaman Nayak |
| Sangamanya | Given at the Adi Andhra Mahasabha held in Elluru |

### Religious and Literary Contributions

*   He was drawn to Buddhism and celebrated **Buddha Jayanthi** every year from **1913 to 1937** (first celebrated in 1913 on Vaishaka Shudda Purnima; last celebrated under his leadership on **25th May, 1937**).
*   He wrote **"Vetti Madiga,"** the first Dalit story in Telugu literature.

### Organizations Established

Bhagya Reddy Varma founded a series of organizations as part of the Adi Hindu movement:

| Organization | Year |
|---|---|
| Jagan Mitra Mandali | 1906 |
| Adi Hindu Karyakartala Dalam | 1906 |
| Vaidika Dharma Prachaini Sabha | 1910 |
| Manya Sangam | 1911 |
| Ahimsa Samajam | 1912 |
| Swastik Volunteers Sangam | 1912 |
| Jeeva Raksha Gnana Pracharak Mandali | 1915 |
| Vishwa Gruha Paricharak Sammelanam | 1916 |
| Adi Hindu Social Service League | 1922 |

**Jagan Mitra Mandali (1906):** Established with the aim of spreading awareness among Dalits, promoting educational development, and uniting them.

*   In 1910, a primary school was established at Islamia Bazar under this initiative; many more Adi Hindu Schools followed.
*   In 1929, **Gandhiji visited** the Adi Hindu School established by Bhagya Reddy Varma.
*   At a meeting organized by Bhagya Reddy Varma at **Victory Play Ground, Chaderghat**, Gandhiji warned Hindus that practicing untouchability is a sin and a bad mark for Hinduism.
*   From 1934, the **Nizam government** took over responsibility for **26 Adi Hindu Schools** founded by Bhagya Reddy Varma.
*   Separately, schools for Dalit girls in Hyderabad were first established by **Katta Ramakka** and **Jangam Sarvaiah**; Katta Ramakka started a school in front of her house at Secunderabad Kalva Basthi for Dalit girls.

**Manya Sangam:** Jagan Mitra Mandali (1906) was renamed Manya Sangam in 1911, and later renamed **Adi Hindu Social Service League** in 1922. Valthati Sheshaiah was the president of the Manya Sangam working committee.

Important programs of Manya Sangam:

*   Spreading awareness regarding education.
*   Abolition of the Devadasi and Jogini systems.
*   Abolition of child marriages.
*   Ban of alcohol.
*   Prohibiting meat on special occasions.

Related initiatives:

*   Bhagya Reddy Varma established a **Devadasi eradication organization** to abolish the Devadasi system.
*   In 1915, he established the **Sanga Samskara Nataka Mandali**, having Harijans perform dramas.
*   In 1916, he established the **Vishwa Gruha Paricharika Sammelanam**, which worked for the welfare of maid servants.

### Self-Respect Movement and Adi Andhra Conferences

Bhagya Reddy Varma led self-respect movements for Dalits in both Hyderabad and the Andhra region.

*   In 1917, the **1st Adi Andhra Conference** (also called the 1st Pradeshika Panchama Mahajana Sabha) was held in Vijayawada by **Guduru Ramachandra Rao**, with **Bhagya Reddy Varma as president**.
*   At this meeting, he named Dalits as **"Adi Hindus"** and urged them to identify by that name.

### Adi Hindu League Conferences (1921–24)

Four Adi Hindu League Conferences were held in Hyderabad under Bhagya Reddy Varma's leadership between 1921 and 1924.

*   **1st Conference (1921):** Presided over by **Papanna**. **Kusuma Dharmanna**, an attendee, sang the song **"Maa Koddhu Nalla Dorathanam."**
*   **2nd Conference (1922):** Presided over by **Keshav Rao Koratkar**.

### All India Adi Hindu Social Conference (1922)

*   In March 1922, Bhagya Reddy Varma organized the **1st All India Adi Hindu Social Conference** at Residency Bazar, Hyderabad. **M.L. Adaiah** presided over this conference.
*   Due to his sustained efforts, the terms "Panchama" and "Parayalu" were removed from government records — communities began to be officially called **Adi Dravida** (in Tamil regions) and **Adi Andhra** (in Andhra regions), as per a **G.O. issued by the Madras Government on 25th March, 1922**.

### Adi Hindu Sabha and Related Activities (1925)

*   In 1925, Bhagya Reddy Varma organized the **Adi Hindu Sabha**, with **Subedar Sayanna** (prominently known as a leader of the Arundhatis) as president.
*   In 1925, he organized an exhibition of portraits and sculptures created by Adi-Hindus at Residency Bazar, Hyderabad.
*   In 1925, he conducted **Adi Hindu Youth Gymnastic competitions** at Prem Theater Ground, Hyderabad, under the leadership of **Kodi Rammoorthy Nayudu**, to encourage Adi-Hindu youth.
*   When **Plague and Cholera** spread in Hyderabad in 1925, he established **Volunteer Medical Camps** for prevention and treatment.

### National-Level Activities (1927–1931)

*   **1927:** Represented South India at the **All India Downtrodden Castes Conference** held at Allahabad.
*   **March 1927:** Presided over the **Mathangi Sabha** held at Mallepalli, where a resolution was passed banning alcohol.
*   **November 1930:** Attended the **All India Adi Hindu Conference** held at Allahabad.
*   **27–28 September 1931:** Elected president of the **All India Adi Hindu Special Conference** held at Lucknow, attended by representatives from across the country, who demanded **separate constituencies for Dalits**.
    *   At this conference, a unanimous resolution was passed electing **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** as the sole representative of the 9 crore Adi Hindu Samaj of India.
    *   Bhagya Reddy Varma **renounced the title "Varma"** from his name at this conference, after a participant pointed out that the term denoted upper caste.
*   **November 1931:** The **Adi Hindu Political Conference** was held at Bollarum, Secunderabad, presided over by Bhagya Reddy Varma.
    *   **Bandhela Chittaraiah** chaired the Invitation Committee.
    *   **Vemula Kurmaiah**, president of the Andhra State Independent Adijana Conference, inaugurated the conference.
    *   With Ambedkar as leader, resolutions were passed for the **abolition of Vetti** and for the **appointment of Adi Hindus in military and police jobs**.
*   Bhagya Reddy Varma also participated in the **Andhra Mahasabha**, passing several resolutions related to Dalits.
*   Due to his efforts, the **Nizam government officially recorded untouchables as "Adi-Hindus" in the 1931 census**.

### Later Life and Legacy

*   In 1937, he founded the **Jambavarna Seva Samithi**, which worked for the upliftment of Dalits.
*   Bhagya Reddy Varma also ran a **parallel judicial system** in Telangana, conducting **Nyaya Panchayats** at the village level with the help of his disciples.
*   He died in **February 1939**.
*   After his death, his son **M.B. Goutham** established the Adi Hindu Social Service organization.

*   Born in **Ramankola, Ranga Reddy district, in 1875**; completed his studies at Secunderabad.
*   Worked as an office boy, a carpenter, and later as a **Ticket Collector for Nizam Railways**.
*   Spread the principles of **Vaishnavism, Brahma Samaj, and the doctrine of Achala**.
*   Established the **Sunitha Bala Samajam in 1912** at Secunderabad, working for Dalit education, abolition of the Devadasi system, and prohibition of alcohol.

**Adi Hindu Jathiyonnathi Sabha:**

*   Established by Arige Ramaswamy in **1922** to work for the upliftment of Hindu society and the eradication of the Devadasi system.
*   President: **Konda Venkat Swamy**; Secretaries: **Papayya** and **Arige Ramaswamy**.
*   Main aims: opposing the concept of Shudras/Neecha Janma theory, and establishing equality among people.
*   In **1927**, it was renamed the **Adi Hindu Mahasabha**.

Later activities:

*   In 1931, he established the **Arundhatiya Mahasabha**, and on **1st June 1931** conducted the Arundatiya conference at the Reddy hostel of Nizam State.
*   In 1934, contesting on behalf of the Adi Hindu Social Service League, he was elected the **1st Dalit Councillor in the Hyderabad Municipal Corporation**.
*   He was the only Dalit poet to take part in the **Golconda Kavula Sanchika**, published by **Suravaram Pratap Reddy**.

Known as **"Hyderabad Ambedkar,"** B.S. Venkat Rao was born on **11th December, 1898** at Hyderabad. His original name was **Bathula Ashaiah**, and he was popularly known as **"Rao Saheb"** among his followers.

*   Worked at the Nizam government engineering college, and later in the Nizamsagar project department of the Nizam's government.
*   In **1922**, established the **Adi Dravida Sangam**, aimed at eradicating the Devadasi system and bringing awareness and unity among Dalits.
*   In **1927**, founded the **Adi Hindu Mahasabha**, under which he built libraries and temples for Dalits at Ghasmandi, Secunderabad (later renamed **Adeyya Nagar**).
*   Presided over the **Mahar Mahasabha** held at Pune in **May 1936**.
*   In **1936**, established the **Ambedkar Youth League** for the upliftment of Dalit youth.
*   In **1938**, established the **Hyderabad State Depressed Classes Association**.
*   Convinced the Nizam to create the **Scheduled Castes Trust Fund**, with **1 crore rupees** for Dalit development — the first welfare fund of its kind in the country.
*   Established the **Adi Hindu Library**.

### Political Career

| Year | Position |
|---|---|
| 1938 | Secunderabad Cantonment Board member |
| 1939 | Hyderabad Municipal Councillor |
| 1946 | Member of Legislative Assembly (MLA) from local bodies |
| 1947 | Education Minister, Mir Layak Ali cabinet |
| 1952 | Rajya Sabha member from Hyderabad Legislative Assembly |

As recognition for his services, the Nizam awarded him the title **"Khusro-e-Alim."**

concepts.partName: Other Leaders of the Adi-Hindu Movement
concepts.bodyMd:
### M.L. Adeyya

*   Called the **"Bhishma of Dalit Communities."**
*   In **1906**, established a school for Adi Hindus named **"Sir William Barter"** at Secunderabad, on land donated by William Barter.
*   The school was later renamed the **M.L. Adeyya Memorial High School**.

### Peesari Veeranna

*   In 1937, when Gandhiji visited Hyderabad, Peesari Veeranna **opposed the word "Harijan"** used by Gandhiji, arguing that the community should be called Adi-Hindus instead.
*   He fought against **Vetti**, urging villagers not to perform it.

### B. Shyam Sunder

*   Authored the book **"They Burn,"** describing the conditions of Dalits in Hyderabad at the time.
*   **P.R. Venkat Swamy** described his entry into the Dalit movement as "a red-letter day in the history of the depressed classes movement."
*   Presided over the **Depressed Classes Conference** held at Parbhani, Marathwada, on **30th May, 1942**.
*   Convinced the Nizam to contribute **5 lakh rupees** to the people's education trust created by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in Aurangabad.
*   Was part of the Nizam's delegation to France, along with **Moin Nawaz Jung and Zaheer Ahmed**, for matters relating to the formation of the Nizam State.
*   Explained the conditions of Dalits at the **United Nations Security Council** and other international forums.
*   Installed statues of Ambedkar at **Bidar** as a mark of self-respect for Dalits.
*   In **1954**, became president of the **All India Depressed Classes Association**.

### P.R. Venkat Swamy

*   Wrote a book on Telangana's Dalit movement titled **"Our Struggles for Emancipation."**

### Dalit Newspapers

| Newspaper | Details |
|---|---|
| The Panchama (1918) | First Dalit newspaper published in Telangana; English monthly magazine; edited by **J.S. Mathaiah** |
| Bhagya Nagar (1931) | Started by Bhagya Reddy Varma; renamed **Adi Hindu Newspaper** in 1937 |

### Important Literary Works of Dalits

*   **Unnava Lakshmi Narayana** — _Maalapalli_
*   **Boyi Bhimanna** — _Paleru nundi Padmashri varaku_ (Paleru to Padmashri); popularized the term **"Mamalu"** (Mala–Madiga)
*   **Gurram Jashuva** — _Gabbilam_

faqs.e: Bhagya Reddy Varma later worked as a tennis ball boy at a Roman Catholic Brothers' Tennis Court and subsequently as an electrician before joining the Brahma Samaj and Arya Samaj.

faqs.q:
Bhagya Reddy Varma is known by which of the following titles for his role in the Dalit movement?
Consider the following pairs regarding titles conferred on Bhagya Reddy Varma:
(I) Varma – Balaji Krishna Rao
(II) Shiva Shresta – Vaman Nayak
(III) Sangamanya – conferred at the Adi Andhra Mahasabha, Elluru
Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
Who wrote "Vetti Madiga," regarded as the first Dalit story in Telugu literature?
Which organization did Bhagya Reddy Varma establish in 1922, marking the final renamed form of the Jagan Mitra Mandali?
faqs.e: This was the last stage in the organization's evolution — founded as Jagan Mitra Mandali (1906), renamed Manya Sangam (1911), then Adi Hindu Social Service League (1922).

faqs.q: Which organization did Bhagya Reddy Varma establish in 1911, aimed at spreading awareness among Dalits?
faqs.e: Manya Sangam was itself the renamed form of the Jagan Mitra Mandali (founded 1906), and was later renamed the Adi Hindu Social Service League in 1922.

faqs.q: In which year did Bhagya Reddy Varma establish the Jeeva Raksha Gnana Pracharak Mandali?

At which venue did Gandhiji warn Hindus that practicing untouchability is a sin, at a meeting organized by Bhagya Reddy Varma?
From which year did the Nizam government take up responsibility for the 26 Adi Hindu Schools founded by Bhagya Reddy Varma?
Who established the school for Dalit girls in front of her house at Secunderabad Kalva Basthi?
faqs.e: Katta Ramakka and Jangam Sarvaiah were the initial founders of schools for Dalit girls in Hyderabad, prior to Bhagya Reddy Varma's later school-building efforts.

faqs.q:

faqs.e: Kusuma Dharmanna, an attendee at this conference, sang the song "Maa Koddhu Nalla Dorathanam."
